title: How Many?: Adding and Taking Away Single-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Adding and Taking Away Single-Digit Numbers Class 1 Worksheet with Answers (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 5)
standard_code: Class 1, Joyful Mathematics Chapter 5: How Many?
standard_text: Addition and subtraction of single-digit numbers: putting together, taking away, using objects, pictures and number lines (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 1)
meta_desc: Class 1 How Many? worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 5): adding and taking away single-digit numbers with pictures, number lines and stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Put together to add. Take away to subtract.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Add: put groups together and count all, or count on: 5 + 3 → 6, 7, 8.
  • Subtract: take some away and count what is left: 7 − 2 = 5.

Examples

Example

3 + 4

Count on from 4: 5, 6, 7

Answer: 7

Example

9 − 3

Count back 3: 8, 7, 6

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the starting number againCount on from the next number.
Adding when things are taken away'Ate', 'gave away', 'flew away' mean subtract.

faq.q: How can I help my child add?
faq.a: Use real things like spoons or beads and say the number sentence together.

items.q: 3 ducks are in the pond. 1 more duck swims over. How many now?
items.e: Start with 3 and count on 1: 4. There are 4 now.

items.q: Gauri has 2 apples. She gets 2 more. How many now?
items.e: Start with 2 and count on 2: 3, 4. There are 4 now.

items.q: 4 fish are in the tank. 1 more fish is put in. How many now?
items.e: Start with 4 and count on 1: 5. There are 5 now.
Start with 1 and count on 3: 2, 3, 4. There are 4 now.

items.q: Varun has 4 crayons. He gets 2 more. Do we add or take away? How many?
